title: Tuesday
text:
NoteTuesday’s main take-home messages





Setting up pixi as the environment Runnig fastqc and multiqc for the downloaded data. Using containers to run the tools in a reproducible way.




What I did in summaryWhat I have done and learned with pixi environmentWhat I have done and learned about containersUseful links



Pixi environment setups
adding required packages to the pixi environment
run required packages in the pixi environment
used screen (similar to tmux session) to run the pixi environment in the background
worked on the WGS data.
used fastqc and multiqc for the downloaded data.
checked slurm files after submitting the jobs and checked the output files.
used bash scripts to be efficient using differnt tools.
try to organize the files and directories in a better way while working on the server.




logged into the server:

ssh delaramb@kebnekaise.hpc2n.umu.se

download pixi via webget if not installed: wget -qO- https://pixi.sh/install.sh | sh source ~/.bashrc (on the server, linux)
set up the pixi environment:

pixi init  -c conda-forge -c bioconda
toml file is created

adding dependencies (required packages for the pixi environment):

pixi add 
pixi run  to run the package in the pixi environment –help or other flags can be used to check the usage of the package

Note: on other servers such as uppmax or local we can also do 1) pixi sell 2)  –help 3) exit
screen -S 
ctrl + a d to detach the session and ctrl -r  to reattach the session, screen -ls to list the sessions
soft link of the WGS data to my own directory under project_dir (ln -s)
zcat | head -n 10
man can initiate the pixi environment without naming it. so on the same directory the pixi environment can be initiated by just typing pixi init and then adding the required packages.
scrun -A  -t  -n  pixi run  ex: srun -A project_ID -t 15:00 -n 1 pixi run fastqc –noextract -o fastqc data/sampleA_1.fastq.gz data/sampleA_2.fastq.gz
I prefer to have scripts directory and the bash scripts to do the analysis. ex:

#! /bin/bash -l #SBATCH -A project_ID #SBATCH -t 30:00 #SBATCH -n 1
pixi run fastqc -o ../fastqc –noextract ../data/*fastq.gz
remember you might need: chmod+x  to make the script executable.
sbatch  to submit the job to the server.

we used the same approach for the multiQC analysis.




Using seqera for the containers
since we have apptainer installed on the server, then we used it to pull the container from either docker or seqera. ex : apptainer pull vcftools_0.1.17.sif oras://community.wave.seqera.io/library/vcftools:0.1.17–b541aa8d9f9213f9
we should execute the container then ex: apptainer exec vcftools_0.1.17.sif vcftools –version
remember containers are like the 3D photo album, so to use it, we should open the door, get inside then we can see the content of the container. so we should use exec to get inside the container and then run the tools inside the container.
we ran the fastqc and the multiqc using the containers.

title: Wednesday
text:
NoteWednesday’s main take-home messages





Nextflow and how to use it for reproducible research.




What I did in sumamryWhat I learnedUseful links



very basics of nextflow and how to use it for reproducible research.
cp -r   to copy the files and directories recursively to the destination directory.
nextflow receive the input files as channels, they go through processes (the scripts-codes) and then the output files are generated.
In short: process  { directives (containers, available modules to be loaded)
 input: 
     data x

 output:
     output y 

 script:
     """
     this is like a fuction that takes the input and generates the output. 
     """

  u should also specify the workflow for the next flow to know what is the next process after the current process.   
}
introducing the parameters and how to use them in the nextflow script adn workflow.




logged into the server:

ssh delaramb@kebnekaise.hpc2n.umu.se

cp -r   to copy the files and directories recursively to the destination directory.
screen -S nextflow

then set up the pixi environment:
pixi init -c conda-forge -c bioconda (remember the order is important)
toml file is created
adding required dependencies ex. nextflow

below is a simple nextflow (hello.nf)

#!/usr/bin/env nextflow

params.greeting = 'Hello world!' 

process SPLITLETTERS {
    input:
    val x

    output:
    path 'chunk_*'

    script:
    """
    printf '$x' | split -b 6 - chunk_
    """
}

process CONVERTTOUPPER {
    input:
    path y

    output:
    stdout

    script:
    """
    cat $y | tr '[a-z]' '[A-Z]'
    """
}

workflow {
    greeting_ch = Channel.of(params.greeting)
    letters_ch = SPLITLETTERS(greeting_ch)
    results_ch = CONVERTTOUPPER(letters_ch.flatten())
    results_ch.view{ it }
}

run the nextflow file:

pixi run nextflow run hello.nf
since there are jobs in parallel, the output might not nbe in order and the same.

if there is any changes in the nextflow file, then we can run the nextflow file with -resume flag to resume the job from where it was stopped.

pixi run nextflow run hello.nf -resume

if we want to run next flow on another parameter, we can use the –  to run the nextflow file with the new parameter.

pixi run nextflow run hello.nf –greeting “Hello Nextflow!”

pixi run nextflow log (to check the log of the nextflow file, the status of what we have done)
pixi run nextflow clean -f ( since we have work directory created, each time we are runnnign the nextflow, we can clean up these directories for the sake of space and memory.)

pixi run nextflow clean -before  -f remember to check the log at first, it is good and wise to be cautious while deleting files/directories.
